input.prompt: A professional woman seated at her desk in a bright modern office, listening attentively. She is NOT speaking: lips closed throughout, no lip, mouth or jaw movement. Her eyes look directly into the camera lens the entire clip - no downward glance, side glance, gaze shift, eye wandering or half-lidded look. Only 1-2 brief blinks in the whole clip; eyes otherwise open and steady. A neutral attentive expression that never changes. Head, hair and facial motion at the minimum natural level - only faint breathing. No head turns, tilts, nodding, leaning or gestures. Hands stay as in the source image, loosely clasped and still on the desk. Camera locked and stationary: ZERO zoom, push-in, pull-out, pan, tilt, crop, reframing, perspective shift or drift. Facial expression, gaze, head position and framing at the LAST FRAME must match the FIRST FRAME exactly. Preserve her face, hair, wardrobe, skin tone, lighting, contrast, colour, the office and desk objects as shown; do not brighten, lift the shadows or re-grade. Lettering on the wall logo, mug and books unchanged. One continuous locked-off 5-second shot, no cuts.

exposure_correction.why_not: Take 2's raw exposure drift is 13.66% peak / 3.52% mean (take 1 was 2.30 / 1.78), and it is TWO-SIDED: 22 of 121 frames are DARKER than frame 0, down to 1.84% below. Diane's locked correction only ever scales DOWN (all gains <= 1.0, so no highlight clipping is possible). Clamping a two-sided swing leaves residual - a trial correction landed at 1.78% peak, ten times worse than take 1's corrected 0.16%. Since the take is rejected on other grounds, no corrected version was produced for the repo.
exposure_correction.note_for_future_takes: If a future take shows a two-sided exposure swing, Diane's clamp-to-1.0 method is not sufficient on its own. This has not been an issue on any accepted take so far.

By 5 s the desk, mug and notebook are out of frame. This is the identical failure that rejected Diane's take 1.

causation_note: Two explanations are consistent with one sample. (1) The weakened first/last-frame clause - a specific, identifiable regression that maps exactly onto Diane's documented take-1 root cause. (2) Ordinary run-to-run variance: kling/v2-1-pro exposes no seed, take 1 held the camera with a very similar prompt, and nothing else changed. These cannot be separated without another run. The leading hypothesis is (1) because the removed wording is the exact wording that fixed the same failure for Diane.
